summary: Blue Mtn lookout on Blue or Sutherlands Mountain in the Pictou area, on a 2009 DNR list; province-wide decommissioning in 2015 per CBC; no site record found.

facts.status_note: The province's towers were decommissioned in 2015 and dismantled, per CBC News; no source describes this site today.
facts.agency: Nova Scotia Department of Natural Resources

events.note: Listed on a list of Nova Scotia fire towers on the Maritimes Scanning Site, last updated September 18, 2009, as Blue Mtn, on Blue or Sutherlands Mountain.
CBC News reports the province decommissioned its towers in 2015, then dismantled them.

corrections.current: Nova Scotia closed its fire towers in 2013 and had taken them down by 2015 (CBC News); no source says this one still stands.
corrections.proposed: The province's towers were decommissioned in 2015 and dismantled, per CBC News; no source describes this site today.
corrections.why: CBC News gives 2015 as the year of decommissioning, with dismantling after it. The 2013 date appears only in a 2012 provincial plan to replace 19 towers with aerial detection that year; the release does not record any tower coming down in 2013.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 2012 provincial release set 2013 for replacing 19 towers with aerial detection, and 14 towers were to stay in remote areas. CBC News, carried by Yahoo, says the towers were decommissioned in 2015. The record uses the 2015 date because it reports the decommissioning itself; the 2012 release describes only a plan.

The 2009 list places the tower on Blue or Sutherlands Mountain without choosing between the two hills. The Pictou County page and Canada Lookouts both use the name Sutherlands Mountain, so the story uses that name and reports the list's wording.

notes_for_editor: The only tower-specific record is the 2009 DNR list, which is an unofficial scanner-listener compilation. It places the tower on Blue or Sutherlands Mountain, so the site may be either hill. The Pictou County page gives elevation and community for the mountain, not for the tower. No build date, design, height, staffing or fire history was found. The CBC original timed out in fetch_text and WebFetch returned 403, so the decommissioning claim is cited from the Yahoo copy. A YouTube video titled Blue Mountain Fire Tower~Aerial View appeared in search, and a search snippet gives an October 11, 2014 date for its footage, but the fetched page had only the title, so the date is not used. The brief's local_unit is 'Pictou County', but STORY_GUIDE.md bars 'county' for a Canadian tower, so the story says 'the Pictou area'; a human should confirm that wording.
